Peter Büchel (HSLU W) Normal Distribution SA: W04 1 / 63
Recap: Discrete Probability Distribution
Random variable X:Assigns exactly one number to each random
experiment
Regard Xas function
Example: Random variable Xassigns body height in cm to a
randomly chosen person living in Switzerland
Here: Body height is rounded to centimeters
Domain of this random variable X:All people living in Switzerland
Random variable Xcan only take following values ( range )
W X={0,1,2,. . .,500}
Peter Büchel (HSLU W) Normal Distribution SA: W04 2 / 63
Range deliberately too large: All occurring values are included
Set of values consists only of a finite numbers of integers
Such a set is called discrete
Important: Can choose no value between two values of range
The quantity is “holey”
This can be taken as a casual definition of discreet
Peter Büchel (HSLU W) Normal Distribution SA: W04 3 / 63
Random Variable X:Measures height of a randomly chosen person
Now randomly (therefore random variable) choose a person
Name of the person: T abea
Assume: Each name occurs only once, which is of course not the case
Could have chosen AHV (social security) number, which is unique
T abea has height of 166 cm (rounded to cm)
Formulation with random variable:
X(T abea )= 166
Choose another person: T adeo with height of 176 cm
Peter Büchel (HSLU W) Normal Distribution SA: W04 4 / 63Write:
X(T adeo )= 176
Can do this with every person living in Switzerland
Expression:
X= 174
Event of having chosen a person with a rounded height of 174 cm
Speak of a realization x = 174 of X
Difference :Capital and lower case letters:
▶x= 174 is a number
▶X= 174 is a set (people with rounded height 174 cm)
Peter Büchel (HSLU W) Normal Distribution SA: W04 5 / 63
Can assign probability to this event:
P(X= 174)
Calculation: Divide number of people with rounded height of 174 cm
by number of people living in Switzerland

8 750 000
Determine this way all probabilities for xin range of random variable:
P(X= x)
Peter Büchel (HSLU W) Normal Distribution SA: W04 6 / 63
In particular:
P(X= 500)= 0
Because there no person with such a height
Therefore it does not matter if range is way too large
Can determine further probabilities
So:
P(X≤ 170)
▶Probability that randomly chosen person has rounded height of 170 cm
or less
Important: Adding up all probabilities of distribution gives 1:
P(X= 0) + P(X= 1) + . . .+P(X= 499) + P(X= 500)= 1

Peter Büchel (HSLU W) Normal Distribution SA: W04 16 / 63Continuous Measurement Data
In many applications: Measurement data
Measurement data: Can take (theoretically) any value in certain range
Example: Body height (in cm) of humans can take each value in
interval [0,500]
Example:
145.325 986 54 . . .
Prerequisite: Measurements as accurate as possible
Peter Büchel (HSLU W) Normal Distribution SA: W04 17 / 63
Definitions
Range W Xof a random variable: Set of all values Xcan take
Random variable X continuous , if its range W Xis continuous
Continuous: “Continuous” and not “holey”, like set {1,2,3}
Generally: Range is interval (part of number line)
Important continuous value range:
W X=R,R+or[0,1]
Last case: Numbers 0 and 1 and all numbers in between
Peter Büchel (HSLU W) Normal Distribution SA: W04 18 / 63
Point Probability 0
Probability distribution of discrete random variable: Probability
P(X= x)for all possible xin range
Example: P(X= 174)=200 000
8 750 000in Slide 6
But for continuous random variable Xfor all x∈W X:
P(X= x)= 0
Conclusion: Probability distribution of Xcan not be described by
P(X= x)
Peter Büchel (HSLU W) Normal Distribution SA: W04 19 / 63
Example: Height
Measuring height of people
Probability of exactly a height of 168 .254 680 895 434 . . . cm: 0
P(X= 168.254 680 895 434 . . .)= 0
Dashed line in Slide 16:Area 0
But possible: Probability that measurement lies in certain range
(interval)
Peter Büchel (HSLU W) Normal Distribution SA: W04 20 / 63Example: Between 174 and 175 cm:
P(174< X≤ 175)
This probability is no longer 0
Because
P(X= 174)= P(X= 175)= 0
It follows:
P(174< X≤ 175)= P(174≤ X≤ 175)= P(174< X< 175)
New concept: Probability density
